minutes.headline: PACC voted a policy of not paying for programming or other groups' equipment, after the high school offered paid huddle footage.
minutes.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee tried to sort out members' appointment terms ahead of Paul's expected resignation, and accepted the July minutes. The manager reported on studio setup, internet options, and a June financial estimate, and the committee discussed Bartholomew account interest and the studio rent. A no-pay policy was moved and seconded, and the meeting adjourned.

what_happened.line: The committee moved and seconded a policy of not paying for programming, content or other groups' equipment; the vote outcome is not audible in the recording.
The athletic director offered paid footage of high school huddles, and the committee said it has no budget for it.
The committee tried to sort out members' unclear appointment terms ahead of an expected resignation, and placed the terms question on the next agenda.
The committee set its meetings for the first Monday of each month and accepted the July minutes.
On the studio, internet pricing was beyond the budget, and the committee will look for the original lease and wait for a permanent town manager before raising rent.

why_it_matters: The no-pay policy sets what the cable committee's fund will and will not buy, which affects whether outside groups such as school teams can expect paid coverage of their events.
The studio rent and internet costs draw on the cable fund, and the committee has put off any change to the rent until a permanent town manager is in place.
watch_next: The terms question is on the next agenda, and meetings move to the first Monday of each month.
The ending balance is an estimate because finance has not closed out FY24; a final figure is still to come.
